title: Egyptian symbols and the gifts of the Spirit
source_text: Εἶτα τὰ μὲν τῶν Αἰγυπτίων, σεμνολογούντων καὶ τὰ περὶ τῶν ἀλόγων ζῴων καὶ φασκόντων εἶναί τινα αὐτὰ θεοῦ σύμβολα ἢ ὅπως φίλον ὀνομάζειν τοῖς χρηματίζουσιν αὐτῶν προφήταις, φησὶ φαντασίαν ἐξαποστέλλειν τοῖς ταῦτα μεμαθηκόσιν, ὅτι μὴ μάτην μεμύηνται· τὰ δ᾿ ἐν τοῖς ἡμετέροις λόγοις ἀπὸ τοῦ καλουμένου παρὰ τῷ Παύλῳ χαρίσματος ἐν τῷ „διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος“ λόγῳ σοφίας καὶ ἐν τῷ „κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα“ λόγῳ γνώσεως παριστάμενα τοῖς ἐν χριστιανισμῷ πολυμαθέσιν οὐδὲ πεφαντάσθαι μοι ὁ Κέλσος δοκεῖ οὐ μόνον ἀπὸ τούτων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ὧν ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς κατηγορῶν τοῦ συστήματος Χριστιανῶν λέγει, ὡς πάντα μὲν σοφὸν ἀπελαυνόντων τοῦ λόγου τῆς πίστεως αὐτῶν μόνους δὲ ἀνοήτους καὶ τοὺς ἀνδραποδώδεις καλούντων, περὶ ὧν κατὰ καιρὸν εἰσόμεθα. γενόμενοι κατὰ τὸν τόπον.
pass_a_gloss: Then the things of the Egyptians, who speak solemnly even about the irrational animals and assert (φασκόντων) that they are certain symbols (σύμβολα) of a god (θεοῦ), or however it is dear (φίλον) to their so-styled prophets to name them, he says send forth an impression to those who have learned (μεμαθηκόσιν) these things, that they have not been initiated (μεμύηνται) in vain (μάτην). But the things in our words/teachings (λόγοις), presented (παριστάμενα) to the much-learned (πολυμαθέσιν) in Christianity from the gift (χάρισμα) called by Paul, in the 'word of wisdom' (λόγος σοφίας) 'through the Spirit' and in the 'word of knowledge' (λόγος γνώσεως) 'according to the Spirit' (κατὰ τὸ πνεῦμα), Celsus seems to me not even to have imagined (πεφαντάσθαι), not only from these things but also from what he says in what follows when accusing the body (σύστημα) of Christians, as driving away (ἀπελαυνόντων) every wise person (σοφόν) from the word of their faith and calling (καλούντων) only the senseless (ἀνοήτους) and the slavish (ἀνδραποδώδεις); about which we shall know (εἰσόμεθα) in due season (κατὰ καιρόν), having come to the place (τόπος).
pass_b_english: Then he says that the things of the Egyptians, who speak with solemnity even about the irrational animals and claim that they are in some way symbols of a god, or whatever those who are styled their prophets like to call them, give those who have learned these things the impression that they were not initiated in vain.

But as for the things in our teaching that are presented to the deeply learned in Christianity from what Paul calls a gift, in the “word of wisdom” given “through the Spirit” and in the “word of knowledge” given “according to the Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:8), Celsus does not seem to me even to have imagined them. I judge this not only from these remarks but also from what he says later, when he accuses the Christian body of driving every wise man away from the teaching of their faith and inviting only the senseless and the slavish. We shall see about this in due course, when we reach that passage.

choices.choice: Celsus's claim about the Egyptians and his later charge against Christians are both indirect speech in the Greek, so not in quotation marks. 1 Corinthians 12:8 reads ᾧ μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος δίδοται λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα; Origen's phrases 'through the Spirit' and 'according to the Spirit' are taken from it, so they are quoted and Spirit is capitalised (the Holy Spirit). θεοῦ σύμβολα (no article, in the mouth of Egyptian apologists) rendered 'symbols of a god', not 'of God', since it reports pagan religious language; 'symbols of the divine' is a possible sense. χρηματίζουσιν: 'those who are styled (bear the title of)' their prophets. σύστημα rendered 'body' (the Christian association). Celsus's later charge is answered at Book 3.44 onward ('that passage'). εἰσόμεθα, literally 'we shall know', rendered 'we shall see about this'. Origen drops αὐτό from κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα; the wording otherwise matches 1 Corinthians 12:8.
τὰ ... παριστάμενα (passive, from the gift): 'what our teaching sets before' -> 'the things in our teaching that are presented ... from what Paul calls a gift' (teaching was wrongly made the agent)
'that comes' -> 'given' (δίδοται of 1 Corinthians 12:8); 'imagined it' -> 'imagined them' (plural τά)
1 Corinthians 12:8 checked; Celsus's later charge (3.44) correctly left as indirect speech
